title: Outliers
subtitle: Spot a point that doesn't fit the pattern on a scatter graph.

questions.prompt: What is an outlier on a scatter graph?
questions.correct: A point that doesn't fit the pattern of the other points.
questions.feedback: Yes. It's the odd one out, away from the main group.

wrong.label: The highest point on the graph.
wrong.feedback: The highest point can fit the pattern. An outlier is the one that doesn't fit.

wrong.label: A point far away from the other points.
wrong.feedback: A point can be far from the others and still fit the pattern. An outlier is the one that doesn't fit.

wrong.label: A point that shows there is no correlation.
wrong.feedback: One outlier doesn't stop the pattern. It's just one point that doesn't fit.

questions.feedback: Yes. B was a very sunny day, but hardly any ice creams were sold.

wrong.label: A
wrong.feedback: A sold the most ice creams, but it was the sunniest day, so it fits the pattern.

wrong.label: C
wrong.feedback: C sold only 2 boxes, but it wasn't sunny, so it fits the pattern.

wrong.label: D
wrong.feedback: D sits in the middle of the main group.

questions.prompt: One pupil got a much lower mark than the pattern suggests. How many hours did that pupil revise?
questions.feedback: Yes. Go straight down from the outlier to the bottom axis.

wrong.label: 1 hour
wrong.feedback: 1 is that pupil's mark, on the side axis. The question asks for the hours.

wrong.label: 9 hours
wrong.feedback: That pupil revised the most, but their mark fits the pattern.

wrong.label: 5 hours
wrong.feedback: That pupil's mark fits the pattern. Find the one far below the others.

questions.prompt: On a scatter graph of revision and test marks, one pupil revised for 8 hours but got a mark of 2. Which could explain this?
questions.correct: The pupil was ill on the day of the test.
questions.feedback: Yes. Something unusual could explain one point that doesn't fit.

wrong.label: Revising more makes your mark go down.
wrong.feedback: One pupil can't change the pattern. The other points still go up.

wrong.label: Revising doesn't change your mark at all.
wrong.feedback: The other points show that more revision tends to go with higher marks.

wrong.label: All the other pupils' marks were written down wrong.
wrong.feedback: It's only this one point that doesn't fit. The others agree with each other.

questions.prompt: Someone says, "This graph has an outlier, so there is no correlation." Which reply is right?
questions.correct: Ignore the outlier. The other points still show negative correlation.
questions.feedback: Yes. One point that doesn't fit can't stop the pattern.

wrong.label: They're right. An outlier means there is no correlation.
wrong.feedback: One point can't stop a pattern. The other points still go down.

wrong.label: Ignoring the outlier leaves positive correlation.
wrong.feedback: The other points go down, not up.

wrong.label: Negative correlation means every point must sit on one straight line.
wrong.feedback: The points only need to go down overall. They don't have to sit on a line.

points.text: An outlier is a point that doesn't fit the pattern of the other points.
It isn't always the highest or lowest point. Look for the one away from the main group.
Read it like any point, and give only the value the question asks for.
An outlier might be an unusual case, or a mistake made when the data was written down.
Ignore the outlier when you describe the correlation.
